lessons.title: Exercise 1.1 (p.12)
lessons.notes_html:
A rational number is a number that can be written as p/q, where p and q are integers and q is not zero. Whole numbers, integers, fractions and decimals are all rational numbers. On a number line, positive numbers lie to the right of 0 and negative numbers lie to the left of 0.

Formula: Place value = digit x value of its place. The place of a digit tells its value: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, and after the decimal point tenths, hundredths and thousandths.

In this exercise: 1. Represent the following numbers on a number line.; 2. Find the place value of each digit from the following numbers.; 3. Find the place value of the indicated (underlined) digit in the following numbers.

Worked Example: i. 87,364

Formula used: Place value = digit x value of its place.

Step 1: 8 is in the ten thousands place = 8 x 10000 = 80000.

Step 2: 7 is in the thousands place = 7 x 1000 = 7000.

Step 3: 3 is in the hundreds place = 3 x 100 = 300.

Step 4: 6 is in the tens place = 6 x 10 = 60.

Step 5: 4 is in the ones place = 4 x 1 = 4.

Answer: Place values: 80000, 7000, 300, 60, 4.

Worked Example: iii. 2,385

Formula used: Place value = digit x value of its place.

Step 1: 2 is in the thousands place = 2 x 1000 = 2000.

Step 2: 3 is in the hundreds place = 3 x 100 = 300.

Step 3: 8 is in the tens place = 8 x 10 = 80.

Step 4: 5 is in the ones place = 5 x 1 = 5.

Answer: Place values: 2000, 300, 80, 5.

Worked Example: v. 680.984

Formula used: Place value = digit x value of its place.

Step 1: 6 is in the hundreds place = 6 x 100 = 600.

Step 2: 8 is in the tens place = 8 x 10 = 80.

Step 3: 0 is in the ones place = 0 x 1 = 0.

Step 4: 9 is in the tenths place = 9 x 1/10 = 0.9.

Step 5: 8 is in the hundredths place = 8 x 1/100 = 0.08.

Step 6: 4 is in the thousandths place = 4 x 1/1000 = 0.004.

Answer: Place values: 600, 80, 0, 0.9, 0.08, 0.004.

Worked Example: i. 4537 (underlined digit 5)

Formula used: Place value = digit x value of its place.

Step 1: The underlined digit 5 is in the hundreds place.

Step 2: Place value = 5 x 100 = 500.

Answer: 500.

Worked Example: iii. 9247 (underlined digit 2)

Formula used: Place value = digit x value of its place.

Step 1: The underlined digit 2 is in the hundreds place.

Step 2: Place value = 2 x 100 = 200.

Answer: 200.

Worked Example: v. 75912 (underlined digit 5)

Formula used: Place value = digit x value of its place.

Step 1: The underlined digit 5 is in the thousands place.

Step 2: Place value = 5 x 1000 = 5000.

Answer: 5000.

i. 5, 10, and 15

Draw a number line with equal steps of 5 units. Mark 0, then count 5, 10, 15 to the right of 0 and label each mark.

iv. -3, 0, and 4

Draw a number line with steps of 1 unit. Mark 0, then 4 to the right of 0 and -3 to the left of 0, and label each mark.

vii. (printed as a second vi.) 1/2, 3/2, and 5/2

Draw a number line from 0 to 3 with each whole unit divided into 2 equal parts. Mark 1/2 after 0, 3/2 (1 1/2) after 1, and 5/2 (2 1/2) after 2, and label each mark. Note: the book prints this item as a second vi.; it is the seventh item in order.

ix. -3/5, -1/5, 1/5, and 3/5

Draw a number line from -1 to 1 with each whole unit divided into 5 equal parts. Mark -3/5 and -1/5 to the left of 0, and 1/5 and 3/5 to the right of 0, and label each mark.

xii. -2.5, -1.5, -0.5, 0.5

Draw a number line from -3 to 1 with each whole unit divided into 2 equal parts (each part = 0.5). Mark -2.5, -1.5, and -0.5 to the left of 0, and 0.5 to the right of 0, and label each mark.

mcqs.why: The notes state that on a number line positive numbers lie to the right of 0 and negative numbers lie to the left of 0.

mcqs.q: On a number line from 0 to 3 with each unit divided into 2 equal parts, 5/2 is the same as which mixed number?
mcqs.why: 5/2 = 4/2 + 1/2 = 2 + 1/2 = 2 1/2, so 5/2 is marked after 2 on that number line.

mcqs.why: The notes mark -3/5 and -1/5 to the left of 0, and 1/5 and 3/5 to the right of 0, because negative numbers lie left of 0.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.2 (p.17)
lessons.notes_html:
Rounding replaces a number by a nearby simpler number. Significant figures are counted from the first non-zero digit. To round, look at the digit just after the place you keep: if it is 5 or more, increase the kept digit by 1; if it is less than 5, keep the digit as it is. The digits after it become zeros (or are dropped after the decimal point).

In this exercise: 1. Round off the following whole numbers to the given degree of accuracy.; 2. Round off the following integers to the given degree of accuracy.; 3. Round off the following rational numbers to the stated significant figures or decimal places.; 4. Round off the following decimals to the given degree of accuracy.

Worked Example: (i) 4567 to 2 significant figures

Formula used: Rounding rule: next digit 5 or more rounds up; less than 5 stays.

Step 1: First two significant digits are 4 and 5.

Step 2: The digit after them is 6, which is 5 or more, so increase the second digit by 1: 5 + 1 = 6.

Step 3: Replace the remaining digits with zeros.

Answer: 4600.

Worked Example: (vi) 1568 to 3 significant figures

Formula used: Rounding rule: next digit 5 or more rounds up; less than 5 stays.

Step 1: First three significant digits are 1, 5, and 6.

Step 2: The digit after them is 8, which is 5 or more, so increase the third digit by 1: 6 + 1 = 7.

Step 3: Replace the remaining digit with zero.

Answer: 1570.

Worked Example: (iv) 67890 to 3 significant figures

Formula used: Rounding rule: next digit 5 or more rounds up; less than 5 stays.

Step 1: First three significant digits are 6, 7, and 8.

Step 2: The digit after them is 9, which is 5 or more, so increase the third digit by 1: 8 + 1 = 9.

Step 3: Replace the remaining digits with zeros.

Answer: 67900.

Worked Example: (iii) 23/9 to 3 significant figures

Formula used: Rounding rule: next digit 5 or more rounds up; less than 5 stays.

Step 1: Convert to a decimal: 23/9 = 2.555...

Step 2: First three significant digits are 2, 5, and 5.

Step 3: The digit after them is 5, which is 5 or more, so increase the third digit by 1: 5 + 1 = 6.

Answer: 2.56.

Worked Example: (i) 17.8569 to 2 significant figures

Formula used: Rounding rule: next digit 5 or more rounds up; less than 5 stays.

Step 1: First two significant digits are 1 and 7.

Step 2: The digit after them is 8, which is 5 or more, so increase the second digit by 1: 7 + 1 = 8.

Step 3: Drop the remaining digits.

Answer: 18.

Worked Example: (vi) 0.032145 to 2 decimal places

Formula used: Rounding rule: next digit 5 or more rounds up; less than 5 stays.

Step 1: Keep 2 decimal places: 0.03.

Step 2: The digit after the second decimal place is 2, which is less than 5, so the second decimal digit stays 3.

Answer: 0.03.

Note: Note on Exercise 1.2 Q4: the book's answer key as scanned gives different values for Q4 (i), (iii), (iv), and (vi); the answers above follow the unit's own rounding rules step by step (for example 9.87654 to 3 significant figures is 9.88, and 0.032145 to 2 decimal places is 0.03).

lessons.title: Exercise 1.3 (pp.23-24)
lessons.notes_html:
A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. An improper fraction has numerator equal to or greater than the denominator. A mixed number has a whole part and a fraction part. To compare fractions, make the denominators the same first.

Formula: Mixed number = whole part + fraction part; Improper fraction = (whole x denominator + numerator) / denominator.

In this exercise: 4. Identify the following fractions (Proper, Improper, or Mixed).; 5. Convert fractions as directed.; 6. Compare using symbols (=, <, >, <=, >=).; 7. Arrange the following in ascending order.; 8. Arrange the following in descending order (p.24).

Worked Example: 1. Find the HCF of 36 and 48

Formula used: Improper fraction = (whole x denominator + numerator) / denominator.

Step 1: Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36.

Step 2: Factors of 48: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48.

Step 3: Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.

Step 4: The highest common factor is 12.

Answer: HCF = 12.

Worked Example: (v) 18/13 into a mixed fraction

Formula used: Improper fraction = (whole x denominator + numerator) / denominator.

Step 1: Divide 18 by 13: 18 = 13 x 1 + 5.

Step 2: The quotient 1 is the whole part and the remainder 5 stays over 13.

Answer: 1 5/13.

Worked Example: (vi) 3/5 and 5/8

Formula used: Improper fraction = (whole x denominator + numerator) / denominator.

Step 1: Convert to decimals: 3/5 = 0.6 and 5/8 = 0.625.

Step 2: 0.6 < 0.625.

Answer: 3/5 < 5/8.

Worked Example: (iii) -7, -2, 4, -5, 0

Formula used: Improper fraction = (whole x denominator + numerator) / denominator.

Step 1: Negatives come first, most negative first: -7 < -5 < -2 < 0 < 4.

Answer: -7, -5, -2, 0, 4.

Worked Example: (i) 435, 278, 899, 643

Formula used: Improper fraction = (whole x denominator + numerator) / denominator.

Step 1: Compare hundreds digits: 899 > 643 > 435 > 278.

Answer: 899, 643, 435, 278.

Worked Example: (viii) 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.0625

Formula used: Improper fraction = (whole x denominator + numerator) / denominator.

Step 1: Compare thousandths: 0.375 > 0.25 > 0.125 > 0.0625.

Answer: 0.375, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625.

(i) 5/8

Proper fraction: the numerator (5) is smaller than the denominator (8).

(iii) 12/5

Improper fraction: the numerator (12) is greater than the denominator (5).

(v) 24/32

Proper fraction: the numerator (24) is smaller than the denominator (32).

(vi) 5 2/9

Mixed fraction: a whole number (5) with a proper fraction (2/9).

(viii) 3/16

Proper fraction: the numerator (3) is smaller than the denominator (16).

mcqs.q: A proper fraction is a fraction in which:
options: The numerator is greater than the denominator
The numerator is smaller than the denominator
There is a whole part and a fraction part
mcqs.why: The notes define a proper fraction as a fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator.

mcqs.q: What type of fraction is 5/8?
mcqs.why: In 5/8 the numerator 5 is smaller than the denominator 8, so by the definition it is a proper fraction.

mcqs.q: What type of fraction is 12/5?
mcqs.why: In 12/5 the numerator 12 is greater than the denominator 5, so by the definition it is an improper fraction.

mcqs.q: What type of number is 5 2/9?
mcqs.why: 5 2/9 has a whole number part 5 with a proper fraction part 2/9, so the notes call it a mixed fraction.

mcqs.q: Find the HCF of 36 and 48.
mcqs.why: Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Factors of 48: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48. Common factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12, and the highest is 12.

mcqs.q: Convert 18/13 into a mixed fraction.
mcqs.why: Divide 18 by 13: 18 = 13 x 1 + 5. The quotient 1 is the whole part and the remainder 5 stays over 13, giving 1 5/13.

mcqs.q: Compare 3/5 and 5/8. Which statement is correct?
mcqs.why: Convert to decimals: 3/5 = 0.6 and 5/8 = 0.625. Since 0.6 < 0.625, we have 3/5 < 5/8.

mcqs.q: Arrange -7, -2, 4, -5, 0 in ascending order.
mcqs.why: Negatives come first, most negative first: -7 < -5 < -2 < 0 < 4, so the ascending order is -7, -5, -2, 0, 4.

mcqs.q: Arrange 435, 278, 899, 643 in descending order.
mcqs.why: Compare hundreds digits: 899 > 643 > 435 > 278, so the descending order is 899, 643, 435, 278.

mcqs.q: Arrange 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.0625 in descending order.
mcqs.why: Compare thousandths: 0.375 > 0.25 > 0.125 > 0.0625, so the descending order is 0.375, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.4 (p.29)
lessons.notes_html:
Rational numbers follow three laws. Commutative: a + b = b + a and a x b = b x a. Associative: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c) and (a x b) x c = a x (b x c). Distributive: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c. To verify a law, work out the left-hand side and the right-hand side separately and check that they are equal.

In this exercise: 1. Verify Associative Property w.r.t. Addition and Multiplication.; 2. Verify Commutative Property w.r.t. Addition and Multiplication.; 3. Verify distributive property of rational numbers w.r.t. multiplication over addition/subtraction.

Worked Example: (i) (-1/2 + 1/3) + 1/4 = -1/2 + (1/3 + 1/4) [minus restored on the right]

Formula used: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c.

Step 1: LHS: -1/2 + 1/3 = -3/6 + 2/6 = -1/6.

Step 2: LHS: -1/6 + 1/4 = -2/12 + 3/12 = 1/12.

Step 3: RHS: 1/3 + 1/4 = 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12.

Step 4: RHS: -1/2 + 7/12 = -6/12 + 7/12 = 1/12.

Step 5: LHS = RHS = 1/12, so the associative property is verified.

Answer: Verified: both sides equal 1/12. As printed (right-hand side +1/2), the right side would be 13/12 and the equation would not balance.

Worked Example: (iv) (1/2 x 2/3) x 3/4 = 1/2 x (2/3 x 3/4)

Formula used: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c.

Step 1: LHS: 1/2 x 2/3 = 2/6 = 1/3.

Step 2: LHS: 1/3 x 3/4 = 3/12 = 1/4.

Step 3: RHS: 2/3 x 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2.

Step 4: RHS: 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4.

Step 5: LHS = RHS = 1/4, so the associative property is verified.

Answer: Verified: both sides equal 1/4.

Worked Example: (ii) -4/9 + 5/6 = 5/6 + -4/9

Formula used: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c.

Step 1: LHS: -4/9 + 5/6 = -8/18 + 15/18 = 7/18.

Step 2: RHS: 5/6 + -4/9 = 15/18 - 8/18 = 7/18.

Step 3: LHS = RHS, so the commutative property is verified.

Answer: Verified: both sides equal 7/18.

Worked Example: (v) 4/9 x 7/10 = 7/10 x 4/9

Formula used: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c.

Step 1: LHS: 4/9 x 7/10 = 28/90 = 14/45.

Step 2: RHS: 7/10 x 4/9 = 28/90 = 14/45.

Step 3: LHS = RHS, so the commutative property is verified.

Answer: Verified: both sides equal 14/45.

Worked Example: (iii) 3/4 x (1/2 + 3/7) = 3/4 x 1/2 + 3/4 x 3/7

Formula used: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c.

Step 1: LHS: 1/2 + 3/7 = 7/14 + 6/14 = 13/14.

Step 2: LHS: 3/4 x 13/14 = 39/56.

Step 3: RHS: 3/4 x 1/2 = 3/8 and 3/4 x 3/7 = 9/28.

Step 4: RHS: 3/8 + 9/28 = 21/56 + 18/56 = 39/56.

Step 5: LHS = RHS, so the distributive property is verified.

Answer: Verified: both sides equal 39/56.

Worked Example: (vi) 3/4 x (1/2 - 3/7) = 3/4 x 1/2 - 3/4 x 3/7

Formula used: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c.

Step 1: LHS: 1/2 - 3/7 = 7/14 - 6/14 = 1/14.

Step 2: LHS: 3/4 x 1/14 = 3/56.

Step 3: RHS: 3/4 x 1/2 = 3/8 and 3/4 x 3/7 = 9/28.

Step 4: RHS: 3/8 - 9/28 = 21/56 - 18/56 = 3/56.

Step 5: LHS = RHS, so the distributive property is verified.

Answer: Verified: both sides equal 3/56.

Note: Flag: Exercise 1.4 Q1 (i) and (ii) as printed do not balance, because the first term on the right-hand side is printed without its minus sign (verified at 300 dpi). The verifications below restore the minus sign on the right-hand side, which is the only reading under which the associative property is being tested; the book's own worked Example 1.45 (p.24) drops the minus on both sides and so balances at 13/12.

mcqs.q: Which statement is the commutative law for addition of rational numbers?
options: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c
mcqs.why: The notes state the commutative law as a + b = b + a and a x b = b x a, so for addition it is a + b = b + a.

mcqs.q: Which statement is the associative law for addition?
options: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c
(a x b) x c = a + (b + c)
mcqs.why: The notes state the associative law as (a + b) + c = a + (b + c) and (a x b) x c = a x (b x c).

mcqs.q: Which statement is the distributive law?
options: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c
a x b = b x a
a x (b + c) = a + b + c
mcqs.why: The notes state the distributive law as a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c, multiplying a by each term inside the bracket.

mcqs.q: What is the value of (-1/2 + 1/3) + 1/4?
mcqs.why: LHS: -1/2 + 1/3 = -3/6 + 2/6 = -1/6. Then -1/6 + 1/4 = -2/12 + 3/12 = 1/12, which also equals the right-hand side.

mcqs.q: What is the value of (1/2 x 2/3) x 3/4?
mcqs.why: LHS: 1/2 x 2/3 = 1/3, then 1/3 x 3/4 = 3/12 = 1/4. RHS also gives 1/4, verifying the associative law.

mcqs.q: What is -4/9 + 5/6?
mcqs.why: -4/9 + 5/6 = -8/18 + 15/18 = 7/18. The same result is obtained for 5/6 + -4/9, verifying commutativity.

mcqs.q: What is 4/9 x 7/10?
mcqs.why: 4/9 x 7/10 = 28/90 = 14/45 after dividing numerator and denominator by 2, and 7/10 x 4/9 gives the same value.

mcqs.q: To verify a law for rational numbers, what should you do?
options: Work out only the left-hand side
Work out the left-hand side and right-hand side separately and check they are equal
Change the numbers until they match
Work out only the right-hand side
mcqs.why: The notes state: to verify a law, work out the left-hand side and the right-hand side separately and check that they are equal.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.5 (p.31) - Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems use the same operations on rational numbers. Read the question, write the numbers, choose the operation, and work step by step. Always write the unit in the answer.

Worked Example: 1. Sarah walks 2/5 kilometers in the morning and 3/7 kilometers in the evening. How much distance does she walk in total?

Formula used: Choose the operation from the words of the question, then calculate step by step.

Step 1: Total distance = 2/5 + 3/7.

Step 2: LCM of 5 and 7 is 35.

Step 3: 2/5 = 14/35 and 3/7 = 15/35.

Step 4: 14/35 + 15/35 = 29/35.

Answer: Sarah walks 29/35 kilometers in total.

Worked Example: 2. A tank is 3/8 filled with water. Another 1/4 of the tank is filled. What fraction of the tank is now filled?

Formula used: Choose the operation from the words of the question, then calculate step by step.

Step 1: Fraction now filled = 3/8 + 1/4.

Step 2: 1/4 = 2/8.

Step 3: 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8.

Answer: 5/8 of the tank is now filled.

Worked Example: 3. A ribbon is 7/8 meters long. If 3/8 meters is cut off, how much ribbon remains?

Formula used: Choose the operation from the words of the question, then calculate step by step.

Step 1: Remaining ribbon = 7/8 - 3/8.

Step 2: 7/8 - 3/8 = 4/8 = 1/2.

Answer: 1/2 meter of ribbon remains.

Worked Example: 5. A piece of marble is 2/3 metres wide and 3/4 metres long. What is its area?

Formula used: Choose the operation from the words of the question, then calculate step by step.

Step 1: Area = length x width = 3/4 x 2/3.

Step 2: 3/4 x 2/3 = 6/12 = 1/2.

Answer: The area is 1/2 square metres.

Worked Example: 6. A car consumes 1/8 litre of fuel per kilometer. How much fuel will it consume for 3/5 kilometers?

Formula used: Choose the operation from the words of the question, then calculate step by step.

Step 1: Fuel consumed = 1/8 x 3/5.

Step 2: 1/8 x 3/5 = 3/40.

Answer: The car will consume 3/40 litre of fuel.

Worked Example: 7. A chocolate cake weighs 3/4 kilograms. If each serving is 1/8 kilograms, how many servings are in the chocolate cake?

Formula used: Choose the operation from the words of the question, then calculate step by step.

Step 1: Number of servings = 3/4 divided by 1/8.

Step 2: 3/4 divided by 1/8 = 3/4 x 8/1 = 24/4 = 6.

Answer: There are 6 servings in the chocolate cake.

mcqs.q: Sarah walks 2/5 km in the morning and 3/7 km in the evening. How much does she walk in total?
A tank is 3/8 filled with water. Another 1/4 of the tank is filled. What fraction is now filled?
mcqs.why: Fraction now filled = 3/8 + 1/4. Since 1/4 = 2/8, we get 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8 of the tank.

mcqs.q: A ribbon is 7/8 m long. If 3/8 m is cut off, how much ribbon remains?
mcqs.why: Remaining ribbon = 7/8 - 3/8 = 4/8 = 1/2 m after simplifying 4/8 by dividing by 4.

mcqs.q: A piece of marble is 2/3 m wide and 3/4 m long. What is its area?
mcqs.why: Area = length x width = 3/4 x 2/3 = 6/12 = 1/2 square metres after simplifying 6/12 by dividing by 6.

mcqs.q: A car consumes 1/8 litre of fuel per kilometre. How much fuel will it consume for 3/5 kilometres?
mcqs.why: Fuel consumed = 1/8 x 3/5 = 3/40 litre, multiplying numerators 1 x 3 = 3 and denominators 8 x 5 = 40.

mcqs.q: A chocolate cake weighs 3/4 kg. If each serving is 1/8 kg, how many servings are in the cake?
mcqs.why: Number of servings = 3/4 divided by 1/8 = 3/4 x 8/1 = 24/4 = 6 servings.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 5 and 7 used when adding 2/5 and 3/7?

lessons.title: Review Exercise 1 (pp.31-32)
lessons.notes_html:
Review of Unit 1: rational numbers, number line, place value, rounding, fraction types and the commutative, associative and distributive laws.

In this exercise: 1. Choose the correct options.

Worked Example: 2. In 0.4567, what is the place value of 6?

Formula used: See the formulas in Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: In 0.4567, the digits after the decimal point are: 4 tenths, 5 hundredths, 6 thousandths, 7 ten-thousandths.

Step 2: The digit 6 is in the thousandths place.

Step 3: Place value = 6 x 1/1000 = 0.006.

Answer: 0.006.

Worked Example: 3. In 89.0563, what is the place value of 5 and 6?

Formula used: See the formulas in Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: In 89.0563, the digits after the decimal point are: 0 tenths, 5 hundredths, 6 thousandths, 3 ten-thousandths.

Step 2: The digit 5 is in the hundredths place: 5 x 1/100 = 0.05.

Step 3: The digit 6 is in the thousandths place: 6 x 1/1000 = 0.006.

Answer: Place value of 5 is 0.05 and place value of 6 is 0.006.

Worked Example: 4. Identify the place value of 3 in 23,465.

Formula used: See the formulas in Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: In 23,465, the digit 3 is in the thousands place.

Step 2: Place value = 3 x 1000 = 3000.

Answer: 3000.

Worked Example: 6. Round off 93,425 to the nearest ten thousand.

Formula used: See the formulas in Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: The digit in the ten thousands place is 9.

Step 2: The digit to its right (thousands place) is 3, which is less than 5, so keep the ten thousands digit as it is.

Step 3: Replace the digits to the right with zeros.

Answer: 90,000.

Worked Example: 7. A water tank is 7/8 full. If 5/12 of the water is used for irrigation, how much water remains?

Formula used: See the formulas in Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: Water remaining = 7/8 - 5/12.

Step 2: LCM of 8 and 12 is 24.

Step 3: 7/8 = 21/24 and 5/12 = 10/24.

Step 4: 21/24 - 10/24 = 11/24.

Answer: 11/24 of the water remains.

Worked Example: 8. A rectangular field is 3/5 km long and 4/7 km wide. What is the area of the field?

Formula used: See the formulas in Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: Area = length x width = 3/5 x 4/7.

Step 2: 3/5 x 4/7 = 12/35.

Answer: The area of the field is 12/35 square kilometers.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.1 (p.37) - Average Rate
lessons.notes_html:
Rate compares a quantity with time or with another unit, for example units per hour or words per minute. Formula: Rate = Total quantity / Total time. For multi-part work in this book, the average rate is the average of the separate rates.

Worked Example: 1. A factory produces 130 units in 4 hours. What is its rate?

Formula used: Rate = Total quantity / Total time.

Step 1: Rate = units divided by hours = 130/4.

Step 2: 130/4 = 32.5.

Answer: The rate is 32.5 units per hour.

Worked Example: 2. Jamal types 80 words in 2 minutes. What is its rate?

Formula used: Rate = Total quantity / Total time.

Step 1: Rate = words divided by minutes = 80/2.

Step 2: 80/2 = 40.

Answer: The rate is 40 words per minute.

Worked Example: 4. A plant grows 10 cm in 5 days. What is its average rate of growth per day?

Formula used: Rate = Total quantity / Total time.

Step 1: Average rate = growth divided by days = 10/5.

Step 2: 10/5 = 2.

Answer: The average rate of growth is 2 cm per day.

Worked Example: 5. A student working part-time earns Rs. 15290 for working 16 days and Rs. 10500 for working another 14 days. Find his average wage rate per day.

Formula used: Rate = Total quantity / Total time.

Step 1: First daily rate = 15290/16 = 955.625 rupees per day.

Step 2: Second daily rate = 10500/14 = 750 rupees per day.

Step 3: Average wage rate = (955.625 + 750)/2 = 1705.625/2 = 852.8125.

Answer: The average wage rate is Rs. 852.8125 per day (the book's answer-key method, the average of the two daily rates). Note: total earnings divided by total days would give (15290 + 10500)/(16 + 14) = 25790/30 = Rs. 859.67 per day; the two methods differ because the two periods have different lengths.

Worked Example: 7. The first day, Riaz reads 50 pages of a novel in 3 hours and 70 pages in 4 hours the next day. What is the average rate of his reading per hour?

Formula used: Rate = Total quantity / Total time.

Step 1: First day rate = 50/3 = 16.67 pages per hour.

Step 2: Second day rate = 70/4 = 17.5 pages per hour.

Step 3: Average rate = (16.67 + 17.5)/2 = 34.17/2 = 17.08 pages per hour (the book's average-of-rates method, as in Q5 and Q8).

Answer: The average rate of reading is about 17.08 pages per hour. Note: total pages divided by total hours would give 120/7 = 17.14 pages per hour; the answer key as scanned reads 17.83, which matches neither method and is treated as a key misprint.

Worked Example: 8. Nawaz is going to Karachi in a car. He drives 450 km in 5 hours and after a stay started his journey and completed 236 km in 4 hours. What is the average rate of his car speed per hour?

Formula used: Rate = Total quantity / Total time.

Step 1: First part speed = 450/5 = 90 km per hour.

Step 2: Second part speed = 236/4 = 59 km per hour.

Step 3: Average rate = (90 + 59)/2 = 149/2 = 74.5 km per hour (the book's average-of-rates method, matching the answer key).

Answer: The average rate of his car speed is 74.5 km per hour. Note: total distance divided by total time would give 686/9 = 76.22 km per hour.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.2 (p.39) - Increasing and Decreasing Quantities
lessons.notes_html:
A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, written as a : b. To increase or decrease a quantity in a given ratio, first find one part, then multiply. Formula: One part = Total / Sum of ratio parts; Each share = One part x its ratio number.

In this exercise: 1. Find the new increasing and decreasing quantity in the following:

Worked Example: (i) Increase 45 min in the ratio 4:3.

Formula used: One part = Total / Sum of ratio parts.

Step 1: New quantity = 4/3 x 45.

Step 2: 4/3 x 45 = 4 x 15 = 60 min.

Step 3: Increase = 60 - 45 = 15 min (the answer-key figure).

Answer: The new quantity is 60 minutes (an increase of 15 minutes).

Worked Example: (iii) Increase 855 km in the ratio 7:5.

Formula used: One part = Total / Sum of ratio parts.

Step 1: New quantity = 7/5 x 855.

Step 2: 7/5 x 855 = 7 x 171 = 1197 km.

Step 3: Increase = 1197 - 855 = 342 km (the answer-key figure).

Answer: The new quantity is 1197 km (an increase of 342 km).

Worked Example: (v) Decrease 660 m in the ratio 5:6.

Formula used: One part = Total / Sum of ratio parts.

Step 1: New quantity = 5/6 x 660.

Step 2: 5/6 x 660 = 5 x 110 = 550 m.

Step 3: Decrease = 660 - 550 = 110 m (the answer-key figure).

Answer: The new quantity is 550 m (a decrease of 110 m).

Worked Example: 2. The price of a shirt rises from Rs. 1500 to Rs. 2500. In what ratio does the price increase?

Formula used: One part = Total / Sum of ratio parts.

Step 1: The ratio of the old price to the new price is 1500:2500.

Step 2: Divide both by 500: 1500/500 = 3 and 2500/500 = 5.

Step 3: So the ratio is 3:5 (old:new), matching the answer key.

Answer: The price increases in the ratio 3:5 (old price:new price; new:old is 5:3).

Worked Example: 4. Huzaifa and Musfira are two siblings; they obtained marks in the ratio 8:7. If Musfira obtained 72 marks, find the marks of Huzaifa.

Formula used: One part = Total / Sum of ratio parts.

Step 1: Huzaifa's marks : Musfira's marks = 8:7.

Step 2: So Huzaifa's marks = 8/7 x 72 = 576/7 = 82.29 marks.

Answer: Huzaifa obtained 576/7 = 82.29 marks as printed. Flag: this is not a whole number of marks, and the book's answer key gives 63, which is 7/8 x 72 - the value for the reversed ratio 7:8. The printed ratio (8:7) and marks (72) are inconsistent with the key; neither has been silently changed.

Worked Example: 6. Riaz has an IT shop, in which the selling ratio of desktop to laptop is 2:5. If he sold 35 laptops, find the number of desktops sold.

Formula used: One part = Total / Sum of ratio parts.

Step 1: Desktops : laptops = 2:5.

Step 2: Number of desktops = 2/5 x 35.

Step 3: 2/5 x 35 = 2 x 7 = 14.

Answer: 14 desktops were sold.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.3 (p.43) - Proportion
lessons.notes_html:
Four numbers a, b, c, d are in proportion when a : b = c : d. In a proportion, the product of the extremes equals the product of the means. Formula: a x d = b x c. Use this formula to check a proportion and to find an unknown value.

In this exercise: 1. Check whether the following are proportions or not.; 2. Find the unknown value in the following.

Worked Example: (i) 2:3 and 8:12

Formula used: In a : b = c : d, a x d = b x c.

Step 1: Product of extremes = 2 x 12 = 24.

Step 2: Product of means = 3 x 8 = 24.

Step 3: The products are equal.

Answer: Yes, it is a proportion.

Worked Example: (vi) 7:21 and 4:12

Formula used: In a : b = c : d, a x d = b x c.

Step 1: Product of extremes = 7 x 12 = 84.

Step 2: Product of means = 21 x 4 = 84.

Step 3: The products are equal.

Answer: Yes, it is a proportion.

Worked Example: (iv) 7:x and 14:28

Formula used: In a : b = c : d, a x d = b x c.

Step 1: Product of extremes = product of means: 7 x 28 = x x 14.

Step 2: 196 = 14x.

Step 3: x = 196/14 = 14.

Answer: x = 14.

Worked Example: (ix) 15:5 and x:20

Formula used: In a : b = c : d, a x d = b x c.

Step 1: Product of extremes = product of means: 15 x 20 = 5 x x.

Step 2: 300 = 5x.

Step 3: x = 300/5 = 60.

Answer: x = 60.

Worked Example: 3. A painter paints 300 square feet in 5 hours. How many square feet will he paint in 3 hours at the same rate?

Formula used: In a : b = c : d, a x d = b x c.

Step 1: Rate = 300/5 = 60 square feet per hour.

Step 2: In 3 hours: 60 x 3 = 180 square feet.

Answer: He will paint 180 square feet in 3 hours.

Worked Example: 8. A farmer has enough feed for 1040 cattle for 50 days. How many cattle can be sold so that the same feed will be used for 75 days?

Formula used: In a : b = c : d, a x d = b x c.

Step 1: Total feed = 1040 x 50 = 52000 cattle-days.

Step 2: Cattle that the feed lasts 75 days for = 52000/75 = 693.33.

Step 3: So about 693 cattle can be kept.

Step 4: Cattle that can be sold = 1040 - 693 = 347.

Answer: About 347 cattle can be sold (693 cattle kept; 52000/75 is not a whole number, so the answer is approximate).

mcqs.why: Rate = 300/5 = 60 square feet per hour, dividing the total area 300 by the total time 5 hours.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.1 (pp.49-50) - Cost Price, Selling Price, Profit, Loss and Discount
lessons.notes_html:
Cost price (CP) is the price at which an article is bought. Selling price (SP) is the price at which it is sold. Formula: Profit = SP - CP (when SP is greater); Loss = CP - SP (when CP is greater); Profit % = Profit / CP x 100; Loss % = Loss / CP x 100. Discount is taken off the marked price: Formula: Sale price = Marked price - Discount.

In this exercise: 1. Identify and differentiate the cost price and selling price in the following questions.

Worked Example: (i) A bookstore buys a used novel for Rs. 250 and gives it to a customer for Rs. 350.

Formula used: Profit = SP - CP; Loss = CP - SP; Profit % = Profit / CP x 100.

Step 1: Cost price is what the seller paid to buy the item: Rs. 250.

Step 2: Selling price is what the buyer paid: Rs. 350.

Step 3: Profit = selling price - cost price = 350 - 250 = Rs. 100.

Answer: Cost price = Rs. 250 (what the bookstore paid); selling price = Rs. 350 (what the customer paid). The bookstore makes a profit of Rs. 100.

Worked Example: 2. Mirza bought a carton of milk for Rs. 80 from the wholesale market. He sold it for Rs. 90. How much profit or loss did he make?

Formula used: Profit = SP - CP; Loss = CP - SP; Profit % = Profit / CP x 100.

Step 1: Cost price = Rs. 80, selling price = Rs. 90.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.2 (p.57) - Tax, GST, VAT and Commission
lessons.notes_html:
GST and VAT are taxes added to the price of goods and services. Formula: Tax amount = Price x Tax rate / 100; Price with tax = Price + Tax amount. Commission is paid on sales: Formula: Commission = Total sales x Commission rate / 100. Income tax is charged in slabs on taxable income, as shown in the unit examples.

Worked Example: 1. Ali has a monthly salary of Rs. 80,000. Calculate his annual income tax liability based on the 2024-2025 tax slabs.

Formula used: Tax amount = Price x Rate / 100; Commission = Sales x Rate / 100.

Step 1: Annual income = 80,000 x 12 = Rs. 960,000.

Step 2: The 2024-2025 slab for income above Rs. 600,000 up to Rs. 1,200,000 is 5% of the amount exceeding Rs. 600,000.

Step 3: Amount exceeding Rs. 600,000 = 960,000 - 600,000 = Rs. 360,000.

Step 4: Tax = 5% of 360,000 = Rs. 18,000.

Answer: His annual income tax liability is Rs. 18,000.

Worked Example: 3. A business owner, Ahmed, earns a monthly income of Rs. 80,000 from his business. Calculate his annual income tax liability based on the 2024-2025 tax slabs.

Formula used: Tax amount = Price x Rate / 100; Commission = Sales x Rate / 100.

Step 1: Annual income = 80,000 x 12 = Rs. 960,000.

Step 2: Slab: 5% of the amount exceeding Rs. 600,000.

Step 3: Amount exceeding Rs. 600,000 = Rs. 360,000.

Step 4: Tax = 5% of 360,000 = Rs. 18,000.

Answer: His annual income tax liability is Rs. 18,000 (same slab computation as Q1; the unit gives one slab table for individuals and businesses).

Worked Example: 5. The property tax on a commercial building is Rs. 120,000 per year. If the tax rate is 12%, find the assessed value of the property.

Formula used: Tax amount = Price x Rate / 100; Commission = Sales x Rate / 100.

Step 1: Assessed value = property tax / tax rate.

Step 2: Assessed value = 120,000 / 12% = 120,000 x 100/12 = Rs. 1,000,000.

Answer: The assessed value of the property is Rs. 1,000,000.

Worked Example: 8. Naseem buys a designer dress for Rs. 25,000. If the GST rate is 18%, calculate the GST amount and the total price he has to pay.

Formula used: Tax amount = Price x Rate / 100; Commission = Sales x Rate / 100.

Step 1: GST amount = 18% x 25,000 = Rs. 4,500.

Step 2: Total price = 25,000 + 4,500 = Rs. 29,500.

Answer: The GST amount is Rs. 4,500 and the total price he has to pay is Rs. 29,500.

Worked Example: 10. (printed 10) If the total amount paid including 18% VAT is Rs. 118,000, what is the original price before VAT?

Formula used: Tax amount = Price x Rate / 100; Commission = Sales x Rate / 100.

Step 1: Original price = total price / (1 + VAT rate).

Step 2: Original price = 118,000 / 1.18 = Rs. 100,000.

Answer: The original price before VAT is Rs. 100,000.

Worked Example: 12. (printed 11, second item so numbered) If a financial advisor earns a 2% commission on an investment of Rs. 400,000, how much commission does the advisor make?

Formula used: Tax amount = Price x Rate / 100; Commission = Sales x Rate / 100.

Step 1: Commission = 400,000 x 2% = Rs. 8,000.

Answer: The advisor makes Rs. 8,000 commission.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.3 (pp.60-61) - Zakat and Ushr
lessons.notes_html:
Zakat is 2.5% of savings and wealth that reach the nisab and are kept for one lunar year. Formula: Zakat = Total wealth x 2.5 / 100 = Total wealth / 40. Ushr is charged on agricultural produce: 10% when the land is watered by rain and 5% when it is watered artificially, as given in the unit.

Worked Example: 1. Mariam has Rs. 900,000 in her bank account, which she has held for over a year. The nisab threshold for zakat is Rs. 87,480. Calculate the amount of zakat Mariam needs to pay.

Formula used: Zakat = Wealth x 2.5 / 100 = Wealth / 40.

Step 1: Her savings (Rs. 900,000) exceed the nisab (Rs. 87,480), so zakat is due.

Step 2: Zakat rate = 2.5%.

Step 3: Zakat = 900,000 x 2.5% = Rs. 22,500.

Answer: Mariam needs to pay Rs. 22,500 as zakat.

Worked Example: 2. Imran owns 150 grams of gold, which he has held for over a year. The nisab for gold is 87.48 grams. Calculate the amount of zakat Imran needs to pay.

Formula used: Zakat = Wealth x 2.5 / 100 = Wealth / 40.

Step 1: His gold (150 grams) exceeds the nisab (87.48 grams), so zakat is due.

Step 2: Zakat rate = 2.5%.

Step 3: Zakat in gold = 150 x 2.5% = 3.75 grams.

Answer: Imran needs to pay zakat of 3.75 grams of gold (its rupee value at the current market price). Flag: the question gives no gold price, so no rupee amount can be computed from the question alone; 2.5% of 150 grams is 3.75 grams.

Worked Example: 3. Laila paid Rs. 15,000 as zakat on her savings. Calculate the total savings amount Laila had if the zakat rate is 2.5%.

Formula used: Zakat = Wealth x 2.5 / 100 = Wealth / 40.

Step 1: Savings x 2.5% = 15,000.

Step 2: Savings = 15,000 / 2.5% = 15,000 x 100/2.5 = Rs. 600,000.

Answer: Laila had Rs. 600,000 in total savings.

Worked Example: 5. Khadija owns a date palm grove that is naturally irrigated by a nearby river. This year, she harvested 2,500 kilograms of dates. Calculate the ushr Khadija needs to pay.

Formula used: Zakat = Wealth x 2.5 / 100 = Wealth / 40.

Step 1: Naturally irrigated crops pay ushr at 10%.

Step 2: Ushr = 2,500 x 10% = 250 kilograms.

Answer: Khadija needs to pay 250 kilograms of dates as ushr.

Worked Example: 6. Yusuf owns a farm where he grows various vegetables. His farm is irrigated by a combination of rainwater and a pump. This year, he harvested 1,000 kilograms of vegetables from the rain-fed part and 2,000 kilograms from the pump-irrigated part. Calculate the total ushr Yusuf needs to pay.

Formula used: Zakat = Wealth x 2.5 / 100 = Wealth / 40.

Step 1: Rain-fed part: 1,000 x 10% = 100 kilograms.

Step 2: Pump-irrigated part: 2,000 x 5% = 100 kilograms.

Step 3: Total ushr = 100 + 100 = 200 kilograms.

Answer: Yusuf needs to pay 200 kilograms of vegetables as total ushr.

Worked Example: 7. Bilal has a farm where he grows vegetables. Part of his farm is naturally irrigated by rain, and the rest is irrigated by a canal. This year, he harvested 3,000 kilograms of vegetables from the naturally irrigated part and 4,000 kilograms from the artificially irrigated part. Calculate the total ushr he needs to pay.

Formula used: Zakat = Wealth x 2.5 / 100 = Wealth / 40.

Step 1: Naturally irrigated part: 3,000 x 10% = 300 kilograms.

Step 2: Artificially irrigated part: 4,000 x 5% = 200 kilograms.

Step 3: Total ushr = 300 + 200 = 500 kilograms.

Answer: Bilal needs to pay 500 kilograms of vegetables as ushr. Note: this question repeats Example 3.21 of the unit word for word (same figures, same answer).

lessons.title: Exercise 4.2 (p.72) - Square Root by Prime Factorization
lessons.notes_html:
To find a square root by prime factorization, write the number as a product of prime factors, make pairs of equal factors, and take one factor from each pair. Formula: Square root = product of one factor from each pair. The same pairing method works for fractions and decimals.

In this exercise: 1. Find the square root of the following by the prime factorization method.; 2. Find the square root of the following fractions by the prime factorization method.; 3. Find the square root of the following decimals by the prime factorization method.

Worked Example: Square root of 36

Formula used: Square root = one factor from each pair of prime factors.

Step 1: Prime factorization: 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3.

Step 2: Take one factor from each pair and multiply.

Answer: The square root of 36 is 6.

Worked Example: Square root of 625

Formula used: Square root = one factor from each pair of prime factors.

Step 1: Prime factorization: 625 = 5 x 5 x 5 x 5.

Step 2: Take one factor from each pair and multiply.

Answer: The square root of 625 is 25.

Worked Example: Square root of 225/324

Formula used: Square root = one factor from each pair of prime factors.

Step 1: Square root of 225 is 15 and square root of 324 is 18.

Step 2: So the square root is 15/18 = 5/6 in lowest terms.

Answer: The square root of 225/324 is 5/6.

Worked Example: Square root of 2116/2209

Formula used: Square root = one factor from each pair of prime factors.

Step 1: Square root of 2116 is 46 and square root of 2209 is 47.

Step 2: So the square root is 46/47.

Answer: The square root of 2116/2209 is 46/47.

Worked Example: Square root of 5.76

Formula used: Square root = one factor from each pair of prime factors.

Step 1: Check: 2.4 x 2.4 = 5.76.

Answer: The square root of 5.76 is 2.4.

Worked Example: Square root of 70.56

Formula used: Square root = one factor from each pair of prime factors.

Step 1: Check: 8.4 x 8.4 = 70.56.

Answer: The square root of 70.56 is 8.4.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.3 (p.75) - Square Root by Division Method
lessons.notes_html:
In the division method, mark the digits in pairs from the decimal point, then divide step by step: each step doubles the quotient to make the new divisor and brings down the next pair. For two decimal places, continue with pairs of zeros after the decimal point.

In this exercise: 1. Find the square root by division method.; 2. Find the square root up to 2 decimal places by division.

Worked Example: Square root of 81 by division method

Formula used: Division method: pair the digits, double the quotient for the next divisor.

Step 1: Group the digits in pairs from the right: 81.

Step 2: Follow the division method step by step; the quotient comes out 9 with remainder 0.

Step 3: Check: 9 x 9 = 81.

Answer: The square root of 81 is 9.

Worked Example: Square root of 2116 by division method

Formula used: Division method: pair the digits, double the quotient for the next divisor.

Step 1: Group the digits in pairs from the right: 2116.

Step 2: Follow the division method step by step; the quotient comes out 46 with remainder 0.

Step 3: Check: 46 x 46 = 2116.

Answer: The square root of 2116 is 46.

Formula used: Division method: pair the digits, double the quotient for the next divisor.

Step 1: Square root of 4 is 2 and square root of 121 is 11.

Answer: The square root of 4/121 is 2/11.

Formula used: Division method: pair the digits, double the quotient for the next divisor.

Step 1: Apply the division method to 2 decimal places.

Step 2: 0.99 x 0.99 = 0.9801 and 0.993 x 0.993 = 0.986049, so the root rounds to 0.99.

Answer: The square root of 0.986 is about 0.99.

Formula used: Division method: pair the digits, double the quotient for the next divisor.

Step 1: Flowers per row = square root of 1600.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.1 (p.82) - Forms of a Set
lessons.notes_html:
A set is a well-defined collection of objects, called its elements. A set can be written in three forms: descriptive form (in words), tabular or roster form (elements listed inside braces { }), and set-builder form (the rule the elements follow, for example {x | x is ...}).

In this exercise: 1. Write the following sets in descriptive form.; 2. Write the following sets in tabular form.; 3. Write the following sets in set builder form.

(i) {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}

The set of the first six natural numbers (counting numbers from 1 to 6).

(v) {3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18}

The set of the first six multiples of 3 (multiples of 3 up to 18).

(iv) {x | x is a prime number between 20 and 30}

{23, 29}.

(i) {11, 13, 15, 17, 19}

{x | x is an odd number between 10 and 20}.

(v) The set of multiples of 5 less than 30.

{x | x is a multiple of 5 and x < 30} = {5, 10, 15, 20, 25}.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.2 (p.87) - Venn Diagrams, Subsets and Supersets
lessons.notes_html:
A Venn diagram shows a set as a circle inside a rectangle that stands for the universal set U. Set A is a subset of B (A subset of B) when every element of A is also in B. A proper subset is a subset that is not equal to the set itself; the set itself is its improper subset. Two sets are equal when they have exactly the same elements, and equivalent when they have the same number of elements.

In this exercise: 1. Represent sets through Venn diagrams, with U = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8} as the universal set.; 2. Identify and differentiate the subset and superset in the following sets.; 3. Identify proper and improper subsets in the following sets and differentiate them.; 4. Write all subsets of the following sets and identify proper and improper subsets.; 5. Every element of B (3, 4, 5) is in A, so B is a subset of A (B is contained in A) and A is a superset of B.

(v) I = set of natural numbers greater than 3 and less than 6 = {4, 5}; J = set of factors of 20 = {1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20}

Every element of I (4, 5) is a factor of 20, so I is a subset of J and J is a superset of I.

Equal and equivalent: both sets have exactly the same elements, and both have 7 elements.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.3 (p.96) - Union, Intersection, Complement and De Morgan's Laws
lessons.notes_html:
Union A union B contains all elements that are in A or in B or in both. Intersection A intersection B contains only the elements common to both. Complement A prime contains the elements of U that are not in A. De Morgan's laws: (A union B) prime = A prime intersection B prime, and (A intersection B) prime = A prime union B prime. Sets with no common element are disjoint; sets with some common elements are overlapping. Note: Venn diagrams in these notes are described in words, so you can draw each region exactly as described.

In this exercise: 1. Find the union of the following sets and represent in a Venn diagram.; 2. Find the intersection of the following sets and represent in a Venn diagram.; 3. Represent the following in Venn diagrams and identify disjoint and overlapping sets.; 4. Find the complement of the given set.; 5. Verify De Morgan's laws.

(i) A = {i, j, k, l, m, n}, B = {p, q, r, s}

A union B = {i, j, k, l, m, n, p, q, r, s}. Venn diagram: two separate circles (no common elements), one containing i, j, k, l, m, n and the other p, q, r, s; the union is everything inside either circle.

(i) P = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 11, 15}, Q = {5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10}

P intersection Q = {5, 6, 7}. Venn diagram: two overlapping circles with 5, 6, 7 in the overlap.

(i) A = {1, 2, 3}, B = {3, 4, 5}

Overlapping sets: they share the element 3. Venn diagram: two overlapping circles with 3 in the overlap.

(ii) U = set of natural numbers, B = set of even numbers. Find B'

B' = the set of odd natural numbers: every natural number that is not even is odd.

(ii) U = {-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4}; A = {0, 1, 2, 3}; B = {-2, -1, 0, 1}

First law: A union B = {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3}; (A union B)' = {-3, 4}. A' = {-3, -2, -1, 4} and B' = {-3, 2, 3, 4}; A' intersection B' = {-3, 4}. So (A union B)' = A' intersection B'. Second law: A intersection B = {0, 1}; (A intersection B)' = {-3, -2, -1, 2, 3, 4}. A' union B' = {-3, -2, -1, 2, 3, 4}. So (A intersection B)' = A' union B'. Both laws verified.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.1 (p.105) - Patterns and Sequences
lessons.notes_html:
A pattern or sequence is a list of numbers following a rule. Find the rule from the first terms: check what is added or subtracted, or what is multiplied or divided, at each step. Then apply the same rule to get the next terms.

In this exercise: 1. Use the first three terms in the pattern to find the next three terms.; 2. Use the pattern rule to make the pattern.; 3. What number is added or subtracted to make the sequence?; 4. What number is multiplied or divided to make the sequence?

Worked Example: (i) 22, 29, 36, ...

Formula used: Next term = apply the same rule (add, subtract, multiply or divide).

Step 1: The difference is 29 - 22 = 7 and 36 - 29 = 7, so add 7 each time.

Step 2: Next terms: 36 + 7 = 43, 43 + 7 = 50, 50 + 7 = 57.

Answer: The next three terms are 43, 50, 57.

Worked Example: (ii) 100, 96, 92, ...

Formula used: Next term = apply the same rule (add, subtract, multiply or divide).

Step 1: The difference is 96 - 100 = -4 and 92 - 96 = -4, so subtract 4 each time.

Step 2: Next terms: 92 - 4 = 88, 88 - 4 = 84, 84 - 4 = 80.

Answer: The next three terms are 88, 84, 80.

Worked Example: (iv) -24, -22, -20, ...

Formula used: Next term = apply the same rule (add, subtract, multiply or divide).

Step 1: The difference is -22 - (-24) = 2 and -20 - (-22) = 2, so add 2 each time.

Step 2: Next terms: -20 + 2 = -18, -18 + 2 = -16, -16 + 2 = -14.

Answer: The next three terms are -18, -16, -14.

Worked Example: (i) Start at 5 and add 11 each time.

Formula used: Next term = apply the same rule (add, subtract, multiply or divide).

Step 1: 5, 5 + 11 = 16, 16 + 11 = 27, 27 + 11 = 38, 38 + 11 = 49.

Answer: The pattern is 5, 16, 27, 38, 49.

Worked Example: (iii) Start at 16 and subtract 1 each time.

Formula used: Next term = apply the same rule (add, subtract, multiply or divide).

Step 1: 16, 15, 14, 13, 12.

Answer: The pattern is 16, 15, 14, 13, 12.

Worked Example: (iv) Start at 243 and divide by 3 each time.

Formula used: Next term = apply the same rule (add, subtract, multiply or divide).

Step 1: 243, 243 / 3 = 81, 81 / 3 = 27, 27 / 3 = 9, 9 / 3 = 3.

Answer: The pattern is 243, 81, 27, 9, 3.

(i) 6, 12, 18, 24, ...

6 is added each time (12 - 6 = 6, 18 - 12 = 6, 24 - 18 = 6).

(iii) 40, 37, 34, 31, ...

3 is subtracted each time (37 - 40 = -3, 34 - 37 = -3, 31 - 34 = -3).

(i) 4, 8, 12, 16, ...

No multiplication or division rule fits: the sequence adds 4 each time (8 - 4 = 4, 12 - 8 = 4, 16 - 12 = 4).

(ii) 9, 18, 27, 36, ...

No multiplication or division rule fits: the sequence adds 9 each time.

(iv) 256, 64, 16, 4, ...

4 is the divisor: 256 / 4 = 64, 64 / 4 = 16, 16 / 4 = 4.

Note: Flag: Exercise 6.1 Q4 (i) and (ii) as printed are addition sequences, not multiplication or division sequences, so no multiplication/division rule fits them; their additive rules are stated. Q4 (iii) as printed ends in 3, but dividing by 3 gives 5 after 15, so the printed 3 is treated as a misprint for 5.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.2 (pp.111-112) - Algebraic Expressions
lessons.notes_html:
An algebraic expression is made of variables (letters), constants (fixed numbers) and coefficients (the numbers multiplied with variables). Each separate part joined by + or - is a term. Terms with the same variable part are like terms; others are unlike terms. A sentence with an equals sign is an equation; an open sentence contains a variable, a closed sentence does not.

In this exercise: 1. Identify variables, constants and coefficients in each of the following algebraic expressions.; 2. Write the number of terms of the following algebraic expressions.; 3. Identify the like and unlike terms in each of the following algebraic expressions.; 4. Identify the open and closed sentences in the following.; 5. Identify and write the names of the algebraic expressions, equations and inequalities in the following.

Worked Example: 6. Shazia is 5 years older than her brother Amjad. Write the ages of Amjad and Shazia in variables and find their ages for various numerical values.

Formula used: Coefficient = the number multiplied with the variable.

Step 1: Let Amjad's age be x years.

Step 2: Then Shazia's age is x + 5 years.

Step 3: For x = 5: Amjad is 5 years old and Shazia is 10 years old.

Step 4: For x = 10: Amjad is 10 years old and Shazia is 15 years old.

Step 5: For x = 15: Amjad is 15 years old and Shazia is 20 years old.

Answer: Amjad's age = x years, Shazia's age = x + 5 years; for example x = 5 gives 5 and 10, x = 10 gives 10 and 15, x = 15 gives 15 and 20.

Worked Example: 7. Naeem bought a geometry box for Rs. 50 more than Waleed. Write the algebraic expression for it and find their purchases for various numerical values.

Formula used: Coefficient = the number multiplied with the variable.

Step 1: Let Waleed's geometry box cost Rs. x.

Step 2: Then Naeem's geometry box costs Rs. (x + 50).

Step 3: For x = 100: Waleed Rs. 100, Naeem Rs. 150.

Step 4: For x = 200: Waleed Rs. 200, Naeem Rs. 250.

Answer: Naeem's cost = Rs. (x + 50) where Waleed's cost is Rs. x; for example x = 100 gives Rs. 150, x = 200 gives Rs. 250.

mcqs.why: Naeem's cost is x + 50; for x = 200 this is 200 + 50 = 250, so Naeem's geometry box costs Rs. 250.

options: It contains the variable x, so its truth depends on the value of x
mcqs.why: An open sentence contains a variable; x + 2 = 3 contains x, so whether it is true depends on the value given to x.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.3 (p.117) - Polynomials
lessons.notes_html:
A polynomial is an algebraic expression in which the powers of the variables are whole numbers (0, 1, 2, ...). A polynomial with one term is a monomial, with two terms a binomial, and with three terms a trinomial. The degree is the highest power of the variable. To add or subtract polynomials, combine only the like terms.

In this exercise: 1. Identify whether each of the following algebraic expressions is a polynomial or not, and why.; 2. Identify the following polynomials as monomials, binomials and trinomials.; 3. Identify the degree of the following polynomials.; 4. Add the following polynomials.; 5. Find the sum of the following polynomials.; 6. Subtract the following polynomials.; 7. Find the difference of the following polynomials (first from second expression, that is, second minus first).

Worked Example: 5x + 2x

Formula used: Degree = highest power of the variable; add only like terms.

Step 1: 5x + 2x = (5 + 2)x = 7x.

Answer: 7x

Worked Example: (-3x - 6y) + (-2x - y)

Formula used: Degree = highest power of the variable; add only like terms.

Step 1: Add x terms: -3x - 2x = -5x.

Step 2: Add y terms: -6y - y = -7y.

Answer: -5x - 7y

Worked Example: 2x^3 - 7x^2 + 4x - 5, x^3 - x + 2x^2 + 8

Formula used: Degree = highest power of the variable; add only like terms.

Step 1: Add x^3 terms: 2x^3 + x^3 = 3x^3.

Step 2: Add x^2 terms: -7x^2 + 2x^2 = -5x^2.

Step 3: Add x terms: 4x - x = 3x.

Step 4: Add constants: -5 + 8 = 3.

Answer: 3x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x + 3

Worked Example: -3x - 2y

Formula used: Degree = highest power of the variable; add only like terms.

Step 1: -3x and 2y are unlike terms, so the difference stays -3x - 2y (the printed box pairs -3x with 2y as separate terms).

Answer: -3x - 2y

Worked Example: -5x^4, 6x^4

Formula used: Degree = highest power of the variable; add only like terms.

Step 1: 6x^4 - (-5x^4) = 6x^4 + 5x^4 = 11x^4.

Answer: 11x^4

Worked Example: 9. Subtract a^3 - 2b^2 + 3a^2b^2 from 4a^3 - 6b^2 - 8a^2b^2.

Formula used: Degree = highest power of the variable; add only like terms.

Step 1: (4a^3 - 6b^2 - 8a^2b^2) - (a^3 - 2b^2 + 3a^2b^2).

Step 2: 4a^3 - a^3 = 3a^3.

Step 3: -6b^2 - (-2b^2) = -4b^2.

Step 4: -8a^2b^2 - 3a^2b^2 = -11a^2b^2.

Answer: 3a^3 - 4b^2 - 11a^2b^2.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.4 (p.121) - Multiplication of Polynomials
lessons.notes_html:
To multiply polynomials, multiply every term of the first polynomial by every term of the second, then add the like terms. In the horizontal method this is done in one line; in the vertical method the polynomials are written one below the other, like ordinary multiplication. Formula: a^m x a^n = a^(m+n).

In this exercise: 1. Multiply the following polynomials by Horizontal Method.; 2. Multiply the following polynomials by Vertical Method.

Worked Example: -3x by 7

Formula used: Multiply every term by every term; a^m x a^n = a^(m+n).

Step 1: -3x x 7 = -21x.

Answer: -21x

Worked Example: 4x^2y by 5xy^2

Formula used: Multiply every term by every term; a^m x a^n = a^(m+n).

Step 1: 4x^2y x 5xy^2 = 20x^3y^3.

Answer: 20x^3y^3

Worked Example: 6x by x^2 + y^2 + 2x

Formula used: Multiply every term by every term; a^m x a^n = a^(m+n).

Step 1: 6x x x^2 = 6x^3.

Step 2: 6x x y^2 = 6xy^2.

Step 3: 6x x 2x = 12x^2.

Answer: 6x^3 + 6xy^2 + 12x^2

Worked Example: (4a - 5)(4a^2 + 3)

Formula used: Multiply every term by every term; a^m x a^n = a^(m+n).

Step 1: 4a x 4a^2 = 16a^3.

Step 2: 4a x 3 = 12a.

Step 3: -5 x 4a^2 = -20a^2.

Step 4: -5 x 3 = -15.

Answer: 16a^3 - 20a^2 + 12a - 15

Worked Example: (5a + 3b)(2a - 3b - 4c)

Formula used: Multiply every term by every term; a^m x a^n = a^(m+n).

Step 1: 5a x 2a = 10a^2; 5a x (-3b) = -15ab; 5a x (-4c) = -20ac.

Step 2: 3b x 2a = 6ab; 3b x (-3b) = -9b^2; 3b x (-4c) = -12bc.

Step 3: Combine: 10a^2 + (-15ab + 6ab) - 20ac - 9b^2 - 12bc = 10a^2 - 9ab - 20ac - 9b^2 - 12bc.

Answer: 10a^2 - 9ab - 20ac - 9b^2 - 12bc

Worked Example: (x + y)(x - y)

Formula used: Multiply every term by every term; a^m x a^n = a^(m+n).

Step 1: (x + y)(x - y) = x^2 - y^2 by the identity (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2.

Answer: x^2 - y^2

mcqs.why: Multiply the numbers and keep the variable: -3x x 7 = -21x, since -3 x 7 = -21 and x stays to the first power.

mcqs.q: In multiplying powers of the same base, the rule a^m x a^n equals:
mcqs.why: The formula given in the notes is a^m x a^n = a^(m+n): keep the same base and add the exponents when multiplying.

mcqs.q: Multiply 6x by (x^2 + y^2 + 2x). The product is:
mcqs.why: Multiply every term: 6x x x^2 = 6x^3; 6x x y^2 = 6xy^2; 6x x 2x = 12x^2. Product: 6x^3 + 6xy^2 + 12x^2.

mcqs.q: Which single multiplication is part of expanding 6x(x^2 + y^2 + 2x)?
mcqs.why: Term by term: 6x x 2x = 12x^(1+1) = 12x^2, using a^m x a^n = a^(m+n) on the x factors.

mcqs.q: Multiply: (4a - 5)(4a^2 + 3) =
mcqs.why: Multiply every term by every term: 4a x 4a^2 = 16a^3; 4a x 3 = 12a; -5 x 4a^2 = -20a^2; -5 x 3 = -15. Total: 16a^3 - 20a^2 + 12a - 15.

mcqs.q: Multiply: (5a + 3b)(2a - 3b - 4c) =
mcqs.why: 5a gives 10a^2 - 15ab - 20ac and 3b gives 6ab - 9b^2 - 12bc; combining -15ab + 6ab = -9ab gives 10a^2 - 9ab - 20ac - 9b^2 - 12bc.

mcqs.q: Multiply: (x + y)(x - y) =
mcqs.why: By the identity (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2 with a = x and b = y: (x + y)(x - y) = x^2 - y^2; the middle terms cancel.

mcqs.q: To multiply two polynomials, you must:
options: Multiply only the first terms together
Multiply every term of the first by every term of the second, then add like terms
mcqs.why: The rule in the notes: multiply every term of the first polynomial by every term of the second, then add the like terms.

mcqs.q: In the vertical method of multiplying polynomials:
options: The polynomials are written one below the other, like ordinary multiplication
Everything is done in one horizontal line
mcqs.why: In the vertical method the polynomials are written one below the other, like ordinary multiplication; the horizontal method does it in one line.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.5 (p.123) - Simplification of Algebraic Expressions
lessons.notes_html:
To simplify an expression, first remove the brackets (a bar or vinculum over terms works exactly like a bracket), then collect the like terms. Remember: a minus sign before a bracket changes the sign of every term inside it.

Worked Example: Simplify: 2(4x - 7) - 5(3x - 1)

Formula used: Remove brackets first, then collect like terms.

Step 1: 2(4x - 7) = 8x - 14.

Step 2: -5(3x - 1) = -15x + 5.

Step 3: 8x - 14 - 15x + 5 = -7x - 9.

Answer: -7x - 9

Worked Example: Simplify: x + (5x - (2x + 1))

Formula used: Remove brackets first, then collect like terms.

Step 1: The bar over 2x + 1 groups it: x + (5x - (2x + 1)).

Step 2: 5x - (2x + 1) = 5x - 2x - 1 = 3x - 1.

Step 3: x + 3x - 1 = 4x - 1.

Answer: 4x - 1

Worked Example: Simplify: 2x + (x - (4x - 3)) + 2x

Formula used: Remove brackets first, then collect like terms.

Step 1: The bar over 4x - 3 groups it: 2x + (x - (4x - 3)) + 2x.

Step 2: x - (4x - 3) = x - 4x + 3 = -3x + 3.

Step 3: 2x + (-3x + 3) + 2x = x + 3.

Answer: x + 3

Worked Example: Simplify: 5x + {4(x - (2y + x)) - 2(3x + (y - 2))}

Formula used: Remove brackets first, then collect like terms.

Step 1: The bars group (2y + x) and (y - 2): 4(x - (2y + x)) = 4(-2y) = -8y.

Step 2: -2(3x + (y - 2)) = -6x - 2y + 4.

Step 3: Inside the braces: -8y - 6x - 2y + 4 = -6x - 10y + 4.

Step 4: 5x + (-6x - 10y + 4) = -x - 10y + 4.

Answer: -x - 10y + 4

Worked Example: Simplify: 2x + [y - 3{2y - (4x - (3x - 2y))}]

Formula used: Remove brackets first, then collect like terms.

Step 1: The bar over 3x - 2y groups it: 4x - (3x - 2y) = x + 2y.

Step 2: 2y - (x + 2y) = -x.

Step 3: y - 3(-x) = y + 3x.

Step 4: 2x + y + 3x = 5x + y.

Answer: 5x + y

Worked Example: Simplify: [x + y - {2x - (5y - (9x - 3x))}]

Formula used: Remove brackets first, then collect like terms.

Step 1: The bar over 9x - 3x groups it: 9x - 3x = 6x.

Step 2: 5y - 6x stays.

Step 3: 2x - (5y - 6x) = 8x - 5y.

Step 4: x + y - (8x - 5y) = -7x + 6y.

Answer: -7x + 6y

Note: Note: the bars (vinculums) in Exercise 6.5 group terms exactly like parentheses; each bar is read as a bracket.

mcqs.why: Remove brackets: 2(4x - 7) = 8x - 14 and -5(3x - 1) = -15x + 5; collect like terms: 8x - 14 - 15x + 5 = -7x - 9.

mcqs.why: Multiply both terms inside by 2: 2 x 4x = 8x and 2 x (-7) = -14, so 2(4x - 7) = 8x - 14.

mcqs.q: In simplifying, -5(3x - 1) equals:
mcqs.why: A minus sign before a bracket changes the sign of every term inside: -5 x 3x = -15x and -5 x (-1) = +5, so -5(3x - 1) = -15x + 5.

mcqs.q: Simplify: x + (5x - (2x + 1)) =
mcqs.why: Work inside out: 5x - (2x + 1) = 5x - 2x - 1 = 3x - 1; then x + 3x - 1 = 4x - 1.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 2x + (x - (4x - 3)) + 2x =
mcqs.why: Innermost first: x - (4x - 3) = x - 4x + 3 = -3x + 3; then 2x + (-3x + 3) + 2x = x + 3.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 2x + [y - 3{2y - (4x - (3x - 2y))}] =
mcqs.why: Step by step: 4x - (3x - 2y) = x + 2y; 2y - (x + 2y) = -x; y - 3(-x) = y + 3x; finally 2x + y + 3x = 5x + y.

mcqs.q: Simplify: [x + y - {2x - (5y - (9x - 3x))}] =
mcqs.why: Inside out: 9x - 3x = 6x; 2x - (5y - 6x) = 8x - 5y; then x + y - (8x - 5y) = -7x + 6y.

mcqs.q: A bar (vinculum) over terms in an expression works:
options: Exactly like a bracket, grouping the terms
mcqs.why: The notes state that a bar or vinculum over terms works exactly like a bracket, so the grouped terms are dealt with first.

mcqs.q: To simplify an algebraic expression, the correct order is:
options: Collect like terms first, then remove brackets
Remove the brackets first, then collect the like terms
mcqs.why: The rule in the notes: first remove the brackets (a minus before a bracket changes every sign inside), then collect the like terms.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.6 (pp.127-128) - Algebraic Identities
lessons.notes_html:
The algebraic identities of this unit are: (a + b) squared = a squared + 2ab + b squared; (a - b) squared = a squared - 2ab + b squared; (a + b)(a - b) = a squared - b squared. Use them to expand products and to evaluate squares quickly, for example 105 squared = (100 + 5) squared.

In this exercise: 1. Complete the following identities.; 2. Expand the following by using identities.; 3. Evaluate the following by using identities.; 4. Find the product of the following by using identities.; 5. Evaluate the following by using identities.; 6. Find the product of the following.; 7. Evaluate the following by using identities.

Worked Example: (6x + 5)^2

lessons.title: Exercise 6.7 (p.130) - Factorization of Algebraic Expressions
lessons.notes_html:
Factorization writes an expression as a product of factors. First take out the common factor of all terms. In the grouping method, group the terms in pairs, take a common factor from each pair, and then take out the common bracket.

In this exercise: 1. Factorize the following (take out the common factor).; 2. Factorize the following (grouping method).

Worked Example: 4x + 16

Formula used: Factorize = take out the common factor first.

Step 1: Common factor 4: 4x + 16 = 4(x + 4).

Answer: 4(x + 4)

Worked Example: 4x^4 - 24x^2

Formula used: Factorize = take out the common factor first.

Step 1: Common factor 4x^2: 4x^4 - 24x^2 = 4x^2(x^2 - 6).

Answer: 4x^2(x^2 - 6)

Worked Example: 3x^2y - 12xy - 18xy^2

Formula used: Factorize = take out the common factor first.

Step 1: Common factor 3xy: 3x^2y - 12xy - 18xy^2 = 3xy(x - 4 - 6y).

Answer: 3xy(x - 4 - 6y)

Worked Example: m^2 - mn + 4m - 4n

Formula used: Factorize = take out the common factor first.

Step 1: Group: m^2 - mn = m(m - n).

Step 2: Group: 4m - 4n = 4(m - n).

Step 3: Common factor (m - n): (m - n)(m + 4).

Answer: (m - n)(m + 4)

Worked Example: 7xz + 5wx + 14zy + 10wy

Formula used: Factorize = take out the common factor first.

Step 1: Group: 7xz + 5wx = x(7z + 5w).

Step 2: Group: 14zy + 10wy = 2y(7z + 5w).

Step 3: Common factor (7z + 5w): (7z + 5w)(x + 2y).

Answer: (7z + 5w)(x + 2y)

Worked Example: 3x^3y^3 - 12x^2y^2 - 18xy

Formula used: Factorize = take out the common factor first.

Step 1: Common factor 3xy.

Answer: 3xy(x^2y^2 - 4xy - 6)

mcqs.q: Factorize: 4x + 16 =
mcqs.why: Take out the common factor 4: 4x + 16 = 4(x + 4); checking back, 4 x x = 4x and 4 x 4 = 16.

mcqs.q: Factorize: 4x^4 - 24x^2 =
mcqs.why: The common factor of both terms is 4x^2: 4x^4 - 24x^2 = 4x^2(x^2 - 6); expanding back gives 4x^4 - 24x^2.

mcqs.q: Factorize: 3x^2y - 12xy - 18xy^2 =
mcqs.why: The common factor of all three terms is 3xy: dividing each term by 3xy gives x, -4 and -6y, so the factorization is 3xy(x - 4 - 6y).

mcqs.q: Factorize by grouping: m^2 - mn + 4m - 4n =
mcqs.why: Group: m^2 - mn = m(m - n) and 4m - 4n = 4(m - n); taking out the common bracket (m - n) gives (m - n)(m + 4).

mcqs.q: In grouping m^2 - mn + 4m - 4n, the first pair m^2 - mn gives:
mcqs.why: The common factor of m^2 and -mn is m, so m^2 - mn = m(m - n), the first step of the grouping method in the notes.

mcqs.q: Factorize by grouping: 7xz + 5wx + 14zy + 10wy =
mcqs.why: Group: 7xz + 5wx = x(7z + 5w) and 14zy + 10wy = 2y(7z + 5w); taking out the common bracket gives (7z + 5w)(x + 2y).

mcqs.q: In grouping 7xz + 5wx + 14zy + 10wy, the second pair 14zy + 10wy gives:
mcqs.why: The common factor of 14zy and 10wy is 2y: 14zy + 10wy = 2y(7z + 5w), matching the bracket from the first pair.

mcqs.q: Factorize: 3x^3y^3 - 12x^2y^2 - 18xy =
mcqs.why: The common factor is 3xy; dividing term by term: 3x^3y^3 / 3xy = x^2y^2, -12x^2y^2 / 3xy = -4xy, -18xy / 3xy = -6, giving 3xy(x^2y^2 - 4xy - 6).

mcqs.q: Factorization means writing an expression as:
mcqs.why: Factorization writes an expression as a product of factors; the first step is to take out the common factor of all the terms.

mcqs.q: In the grouping method of factorization, after grouping terms in pairs and taking a common factor from each pair, you:
options: Remove the brackets and collect terms
mcqs.why: The grouping method: group in pairs, take a common factor from each pair, then take out the common bracket, as in (m - n)(m + 4).

lessons.title: Exercise 6.8 (p.133) - Factorization of Quadratic Expressions
lessons.notes_html:
To factorize a quadratic x squared + bx + c, find two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is b, then split the middle term. Formula: x squared + (p + q)x + pq = (x + p)(x + q). For ax squared + bx + c, find two numbers whose product is a x c and whose sum is b.

In this exercise: 1. Factorize the following.; 2. Factorize the following.; 3. Factorize the following.

Worked Example: x^2 + 5x + 6

Formula used: x^2 + (p+q)x + pq = (x + p)(x + q).

Step 1: Find two numbers with the required product and sum; the factorization is (x + 2)(x + 3).

Answer: (x + 2)(x + 3)

Worked Example: x^2 + 5x - 14

Formula used: x^2 + (p+q)x + pq = (x + p)(x + q).

Step 1: Find two numbers with the required product and sum; the factorization is (x + 7)(x - 2).

Answer: (x + 7)(x - 2)

Worked Example: 2x^2 + 11x + 15

Formula used: x^2 + (p+q)x + pq = (x + p)(x + q).

Step 1: Split the middle term and factor by grouping; the factorization is (2x + 5)(x + 3).

Answer: (2x + 5)(x + 3)

Worked Example: 5x^2 - 4x - 1

Formula used: x^2 + (p+q)x + pq = (x + p)(x + q).

Step 1: Split the middle term and factor by grouping; the factorization is (5x + 1)(x - 1).

Answer: (5x + 1)(x - 1)

Worked Example: 6x^2 + 13x + 5

Formula used: x^2 + (p+q)x + pq = (x + p)(x + q).

Step 1: Split the middle term and factor by grouping; the factorization is (3x + 5)(2x + 1).

Answer: (3x + 5)(2x + 1)

Worked Example: 4x^2 - x - 5

Formula used: x^2 + (p+q)x + pq = (x + p)(x + q).

Step 1: Split the middle term and factor by grouping; the factorization is (4x - 5)(x + 1).

Answer: (4x - 5)(x + 1)

mcqs.q: Factorize: x^2 + 5x + 6 =
mcqs.why: Find two numbers with product 6 and sum 5: 2 and 3. Checking: (x + 2)(x + 3) = x^2 + 3x + 2x + 6 = x^2 + 5x + 6.

mcqs.q: For x^2 + 5x + 6, the two numbers used to split the middle term are:
mcqs.why: The numbers must have product c = 6 and sum b = 5; 2 x 3 = 6 and 2 + 3 = 5, so the numbers are 2 and 3.

mcqs.q: Factorize: x^2 + 5x - 14 =
mcqs.why: Two numbers with product -14 and sum 5 are 7 and -2. Checking: (x + 7)(x - 2) = x^2 - 2x + 7x - 14 = x^2 + 5x - 14.

mcqs.q: Factorize: 2x^2 + 11x + 15 =
mcqs.why: Split the middle term and group. Checking: (2x + 5)(x + 3) = 2x^2 + 6x + 5x + 15 = 2x^2 + 11x + 15.

mcqs.q: Factorize: 5x^2 - 4x - 1 =
mcqs.why: Split the middle term and group. Checking: (5x + 1)(x - 1) = 5x^2 - 5x + x - 1 = 5x^2 - 4x - 1.

mcqs.q: Factorize: 6x^2 + 13x + 5 =
mcqs.why: Split the middle term and group. Checking: (3x + 5)(2x + 1) = 6x^2 + 3x + 10x + 5 = 6x^2 + 13x + 5.

mcqs.q: Factorize: 4x^2 - x - 5 =
mcqs.why: Split the middle term and group. Checking: (4x - 5)(x + 1) = 4x^2 + 4x - 5x - 5 = 4x^2 - x - 5.

mcqs.q: To factorize x^2 + bx + c, you find two numbers whose:
options: Product is b and sum is c
Product is c and sum is b
Difference is c and sum is b
mcqs.why: The rule in the notes: for x^2 + bx + c find two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is b, then split the middle term.

mcqs.q: The formula x^2 + (p + q)x + pq equals:
mcqs.why: The notes give the formula x^2 + (p + q)x + pq = (x + p)(x + q); expanding the right side returns the left side.

options: a + c and whose sum is b
a x c and whose sum is b
b x c and whose sum is a
a x b and whose sum is c
mcqs.why: For ax^2 + bx + c the notes say: find two numbers whose product is a x c and whose sum is b, then split the middle term.

mcqs.why: The review answer in the notes: letters or alphabets used to represent unknown quantities in algebra are called variables.

mcqs.why: The review answer in the notes: in a polynomial the variable power/exponent is a whole number (0, 1, 2, ...).

mcqs.q: A polynomial which contains only three unlike terms is called a:

mcqs.q: The factorization of 1 - 4x^2 is:
mcqs.why: By (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2 in reverse: (1 + 2x)(1 - 2x) = 1 - 4x^2, since 1^2 = 1 and (2x)^2 = 4x^2.

mcqs.q: In the expression 5x + 3, the variable, constant and coefficient are:
mcqs.why: From the review exercise: in 5x + 3 the variable is x, the constant is 3 and the coefficient of x is 5.

mcqs.q: In the expression 4x^2 - 5x + 7, the constant is:

mcqs.q: In the expression 4x^2 - 5x + 7, the coefficients are:
mcqs.why: From the review exercise: the coefficients are 4 (of x^2) and -5 (of x); 7 is the constant, not a coefficient.

mcqs.why: The parts joined by + or - are the terms; 7x - 9y is made of the two terms 7x and -9y, so it has 2 terms.

mcqs.q: The sentence 3y > y is an open sentence because:
mcqs.why: From the review exercise: 3y > y is an open sentence because it contains the variable y, so its truth depends on y's value.

mcqs.q: The sentence 7x < 3x is:

lessons.title: Exercise 7.1 (p.145) - Linear Equations
lessons.notes_html:
A linear equation in one variable has one variable with power 1. To solve it, keep the variable on one side and the numbers on the other: what is added is subtracted, and what is multiplied is divided, on both sides equally. A linear equation in two variables, for example x + y = 10, has many solutions.

In this exercise: 1. Solve the following.; 2. Identify the linear equation in two variables.; 3. Construct a linear equation in two variables for the following.

Worked Example: x - 4 = 3

Formula used: Do the same operation on both sides to isolate the variable.

Step 1: Add 4 to both sides: x = 3 + 4.

Answer: x = 7.

Worked Example: 2x + 1 = x + 2

Formula used: Do the same operation on both sides to isolate the variable.

Step 1: Subtract x from both sides: x + 1 = 2.

Step 2: Subtract 1 from both sides: x = 1.

Answer: x = 1.

Worked Example: 4x - 5 = 3

Formula used: Do the same operation on both sides to isolate the variable.

Step 1: Add 5 to both sides: 4x = 8.

Step 2: Divide both sides by 4: x = 2.

Answer: x = 2.

Worked Example: (2x - 3)/5 = 3

Formula used: Do the same operation on both sides to isolate the variable.

Step 1: Multiply both sides by 5: 2x - 3 = 15.

Step 2: Add 3 to both sides: 2x = 18.

Step 3: Divide both sides by 2: x = 9.

Answer: x = 9.

Worked Example: 5. The length of red electric wire and black electric wire is 35 m. Construct a linear equation in two variables.

Formula used: Do the same operation on both sides to isolate the variable.

Step 1: Let the length of red wire be x metres and of black wire be y metres.

Answer: x + y = 35.

Worked Example: 7. The price of 2 room colors and 5 solar ceiling fans is Rs. 15000. Construct a linear equation in two variables.

Formula used: Do the same operation on both sides to isolate the variable.

Step 1: Let the price of one room color be Rs. x and of one solar ceiling fan be Rs. y.

Answer: 2x + 5y = 15000.

x + y = 2

Yes: two variables, each to power 1.

x - y = 4

Yes: two variables, each to power 1.

The price of 5 apples and 6 mangoes is Rs. 160.

Let the price of one apple be Rs. x and of one mango be Rs. y. Then 5x + 6y = 160.

5 added to a number is equal to twice another number.

Let the numbers be x and y. Then x + 5 = 2y.

7 added to three times a number is equal to 5 times a number reduced by 2.

Let the numbers be x and y. Then 3x + 7 = 5y - 2. Flag: the question asks for an equation in two variables, so the two 'numbers' are taken as two different variables; with one variable it would be 3x + 7 = 5x - 2.

mcqs.why: By definition in the notes, a linear equation in one variable has one variable with power 1.

mcqs.q: Solve: x - 4 = 3
mcqs.why: Add 4 to both sides: x = 3 + 4 = 7. So the solution is x = 7.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2x + 1 = x + 2
mcqs.why: Subtract x from both sides: x + 1 = 2. Subtract 1 from both sides: x = 1.

mcqs.why: Add 5 to both sides: 4x = 8. Divide both sides by 4: x = 8/4 = 2.
Multiply by 5: 2x - 3 = 15. Add 3: 2x = 18. Divide by 2: x = 18/2 = 9.

mcqs.why: Total length is the sum of the two lengths: x + y = 35, as given in the worked example.

mcqs.why: Cost of 2 colors is 2x and cost of 5 fans is 5y, so 2x + 5y = 15000.

mcqs.why: x + y = 2 has two variables x and y, each to power 1, so it is linear in two variables.

mcqs.q: The price of 5 apples and 6 mangoes is Rs. 160. If one apple costs Rs. x and one mango costs Rs. y, what is the equation?
mcqs.why: Cost of 5 apples is 5x and cost of 6 mangoes is 6y, so 5x + 6y = 160.

mcqs.why: 5 added to x gives x + 5, and twice y is 2y, so the equation is x + 5 = 2y.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.3 (pp.150-152) - Coordinate Plane
lessons.notes_html:
On the coordinate plane, a point is written as an ordered pair (x, y). The x-value is the abscissa and the y-value is the ordinate. The plane is divided into four quadrants: I (+, +), II (-, +), III (-, -), IV (+, -). Note: this unit has no Exercise 7.2; section 7.2 gives solving methods with worked examples only.

In this exercise: 4. Identify the abscissa, ordinate and quadrant.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.4 (p.176) - Speed, Distance and Time
lessons.notes_html:
Formulas: Speed = Distance / Time; Distance = Speed x Time; Time = Distance / Speed. Keep the units together: distance in km with time in hours gives speed in km/h; distance in metres with time in seconds gives speed in m/s.

Worked Example: 1. Shazia covered 150 km distance in 2 hours by car. Find the average speed of the car.

Formula used: Speed = Distance / Time; Distance = Speed x Time; Time = Distance / Speed.

Worked Example: 2. A train covered a distance of 260 km for the first 2 hours and then the speed of the train changed and it covered a distance of 160 km for the next 4 hours. Find the average speed of the train.

Formula used: Speed = Distance / Time; Distance = Speed x Time; Time = Distance / Speed.

Step 1: Total distance = 260 + 160 = 420 km.

Step 2: Total time = 2 + 4 = 6 hours.

Step 3: Average speed = 420/6 = 70 km/h.

Answer: 70 km/h.

Worked Example: 4. Usman covers 6 km distance in 40 minutes. Find his speed in km/h.

Formula used: Speed = Distance / Time; Distance = Speed x Time; Time = Distance / Speed.

Formula used: Speed = Distance / Time; Distance = Speed x Time; Time = Distance / Speed.

lessons.title: Exercise 9.1 (p.186) - Quadrilaterals
lessons.notes_html:
A quadrilateral is a closed figure with four sides. In a square and a rhombus all sides are equal; in a rectangle and a parallelogram opposite sides are equal and parallel. A kite has two pairs of adjacent equal sides. Formula: the sum of the four interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360 degrees.

In this exercise: 1. Name the following figures and write the names of their sides which are equal in length.; 2. Find the unknown angles and which angles are equal of the following figures.; 3. Identify the parallel and equal sides of the following figures.

Worked Example: Figure IJKL (parallelogram) with angle L = 75 degrees

Formula used: Sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360 degrees.

Step 1: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so angle J = angle L = 75 degrees.

Step 2: Adjacent angles are supplementary, so angle I = 180 - 75 = 105 degrees and angle K = 180 - 75 = 105 degrees.

Answer: Angles: L = J = 75 degrees, I = K = 105 degrees. Equal pairs: L = J and I = K.

Worked Example: Figure MNOP (parallelogram) with angle P = 70 degrees

Formula used: Sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360 degrees.

Step 1: Opposite angles are equal, so angle N = angle P = 70 degrees.

Step 2: Adjacent angles are supplementary, so angle M = 180 - 70 = 110 degrees and angle O = 180 - 70 = 110 degrees.

Answer: Angles: P = N = 70 degrees, M = O = 110 degrees. Equal pairs: P = N and M = O.

Worked Example: Figure QRST (trapezium, QR parallel to TS) with angle T = 120 degrees and angle S = 110 degrees

Formula used: Sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360 degrees.

Step 1: Angles on the same side between parallel lines are supplementary: angle Q + angle T = 180, so angle Q = 180 - 120 = 60 degrees.

Step 2: Angle R + angle S = 180, so angle R = 180 - 110 = 70 degrees.

Answer: Angles: Q = 60 degrees, R = 70 degrees, T = 120 degrees, S = 110 degrees. No two of these angles are equal.

Worked Example: Figure UVWX (kite) with angle U = 50 degrees and angle X = 115 degrees

Formula used: Sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360 degrees.

Step 1: In a kite the angles at X and V (marked equal in the figure) are equal, so angle V = 115 degrees.

Step 2: The angles of a quadrilateral sum to 360 degrees, so angle W = 360 - 50 - 115 - 115 = 80 degrees.

Answer: Angles: U = 50 degrees, X = V = 115 degrees, W = 80 degrees. Equal pair: X = V.

Figure ABCD

Square: it has four right angles and all four sides equal in length, so AB = BC = CD = DA.
